source.edition: Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition (PlayStation 2, Sidhe, 2008)
source.label: Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition
source.check: A player is kept at his club when the Rugby League Project lists him there in 2008 (first grade, finals and World Club Challenge, or the National Youth Competition), and in a nation when it has him in that nation's 2008 World Cup squad or in one of its 2008 Tests; a name it spells otherwise only with a date of birth on his RLP page like the database's (the same, or one field off in the same year).

conversion.formula: Each player's score at his primary position is the weighted mean of the attributes `weights` gives it (1–10), any attribute at its database default (`defaults`) or omitted (0) left out; then the position's scores among the 2008 clubs' kept players are ranked (mid-rank percentiles, ties sharing one) and read off `reference`, Rugby League 26's overalls at that position (scripts/data/rugby-league-26.json), as many of each 2025 club's best as the 2008 clubs carry per club (`quota`), by linear interpolation; rounded and held to 1–99: his attribute overall. A national squad's player from outside the NRL is placed by his score among the clubs' players at his position. Then each club is shifted: its team rating, the equal-weight mean of the database's five team parts (willingness to attack, attack, defence, flair, support; 1–10), is ranked among the 2008 clubs (mid-rank percentiles, ties sharing one) and read off `clubShift.reference`, the built-in 2025 NRL clubs' strengths, by linear interpolation: its target. Every player of the club moves by the one whole number (`shift`) that brings its lineup's strength closest to the target (of two as close, the smaller move), held to 1–99, so its players keep their order. No result of the season enters either step.

FB.CAT: fields the kicks: the bomb and the grubber are his first duty
FB.SPD: kick returns and support runs cover the length of the field
FB.ACC: returns start from a standstill under the high ball
FB.AGI: beats the first chaser on a return and in broken play
FB.BRK: the kick return is a carry into contact: metres after it start the set
FB.TKL: the last line of defence, one on one
FB.PAS: joins the line as an extra ball-player, a small part of his game
FB.FIT: covers the whole field for eighty minutes

WG.SPD: finishing on the edge is a race to the corner
WG.ACC: beats a defender to the line from a standing start
WG.AGI: steps the last defender in a narrow channel
WG.BRK: carries the ball out of his own end on the early tackles
WG.CAT: takes the cross-field bomb and the kick returns
WG.TKL: defends the edge one on one, with no one outside him
WG.FIT: repeated returns and chases; less than a forward's workload

CE.BRK: runs hard lines into the defence on the edge
CE.SPD: turns a line-break into a try
CE.ACC: hits the gap before it closes
CE.TKL: defends the edge channel, where most attacks are aimed
CE.PAS: gives the winger the last pass
CE.OFF: keeps the ball alive in the tackle for his winger
CE.CAT: takes the pass at speed and the high ball on the edge
CE.FIT: chases and covers; less than a forward's workload

FE.PAS: the second receiver: his passing shapes the attack
FE.KCK: the second kicker, for the attacking kick and the long kick
FE.AGI: his running game is the step off the line
FE.SPD: takes the line on and supports the break
FE.ACC: hits the line from a flat start
FE.BRK: holds his own in contact; not his job
FE.TKL: defends in the line, a channel attacks aim at
FE.CAT: handles under pressure in the line
FE.FIT: eighty minutes of decisions; not a forward's workload

HB.PAS: runs the attack: the long and the short pass
HB.KCK: the main kicker: the last-tackle kick, the grubber, the kick to touch
HB.AGI: runs around the ruck and takes the short side
HB.TKL: defends, usually where the side shields him
HB.CAT: handles every play: a small part, as all of them catch
HB.FIT: involved in every set, at both ends

HK.PAS: passes from dummy-half on nearly every play
HK.TKL: makes more tackles than anyone in the side
HK.CAT: picks the ball up at the ruck
HK.AGG: stands up in the middle of the defence
HK.FIT: at every ruck for most of the game

PR.BRK: the hit-up: metres after contact are his job
PR.OFF: the second-phase play off the hit-up
PR.AGG: dominance in contact, at both ends
PR.CAT: takes the pass into contact; a small part

SR.TKL: edge defence and high tackle counts
SR.BRK: runs the edge lines into contact
SR.SPD: edge running makes breaks a prop never sees
SR.ACC: hits the hole from a short run
SR.AGI: a step on the edge; a small part
SR.CAT: takes the pass on the edge
SR.FIT: plays more minutes than the props

LK.TKL: leads the middle defence, the side's busiest tackler
LK.PAS: the link to the backs: a ball-playing forward
LK.FIT: covers the most ground of the forwards

scales.note: Mean position score (`score`) and attribute (`attributes`) of the 2008 NRL clubs' kept players and of every player the database's Super League XIII clubs list, by competition; `starMean` the mean star value.

clubShift.note: Each club's `team`: its five parts in this order, their mean (`rating`), its target, its lineup's strength unshifted (`strength`) and shifted (`shifted`), and the shift; every player's row ends with his attribute overall and his club's shift (null outside the clubs).
